edits.old: The MongoDB 9.0 manual marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated since 8.0 and says it waits for all orphaned documents in the namespace to be cleaned from a majority of the shard's replica-set members; it does not delete them directly. Alibaba's 2026 upgrade guide says MongoDB 4.4 introduced automatic migration recovery and that cleanupOrphaned can verify the background cleanup. Apply version-specific guidance before using older cleanup loops. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

edits.rationale: The MongoDB manual (v9.0 page pinned) marks cleanupOrphaned deprecated since 8.0 and says it waits for orphan cleanup from a majority of the shard's members, not deleting directly. Alibaba Cloud's upgrade page says 4.4 introduced self-recovery chunk migration and automatic orphan cleanup, and that cleanupOrphaned only confirms background cleanup threads. The generic advice to apply version-specific guidance is a recommendation, not a checkable fact.

edits.old: A range migration updates ownership metadata before the source shard deletes its old copy; the balancer deletes that copy after no open cursors remain. These leftover source copies are orphaned documents and consume disk while range deletion is pending. (high confidence)
edits.new: A range migration updates ownership metadata before the source shard deletes its old copy; the source shard deletes its copy once no open cursors remain on the range. Documents left on the source shard after the metadata update are orphaned documents until they are deleted. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/

evidence.quote: After the source shard completes the update of the metadata, and once there are no open cursors on the range, the source shard deletes its copy of the documents.

edits.rationale: The ordering (metadata update, then deletion after no open cursors) is stated in the balancer procedure. The manual's pinned pages do not say that pending orphans consume disk; only third-party blogs imply it, so that statement is dropped. The orphan definition is supported by the cleanupOrphaned page, which describes orphans awaiting cleanup after migration.

edits.old: Range cleanup can wait on open cursors: the current balancer procedure deletes the source copy only after open cursors on the range are gone. A MongoDB 3.4 forum response explains that an already-being-processed-for-deletion response typically means a query still holds a cursor; the response alone does not establish a failure. (medium confidence)
